_provenance: Authored for Mentor (Phase 10 §1.2/§7 rules check, 8 questions). Standard FIDE Laws of Chess concepts, written in own words. Batch 1 - needs owner review.

questions.q: Which of these stops you from castling?
options: Your king has moved earlier in the game
Your rook is on its starting square
Your opponent has a knight developed
questions.explain: Once the king has moved, it can never castle, even if it returns. You also cannot castle out of check, through an attacked square, or with pieces in between.

questions.q: When can you capture en passant?
options: Any time a pawn is next to an enemy pawn
Right after an enemy pawn moves two squares and lands beside your pawn
Only with a pawn that is on its starting rank
questions.explain: En passant is only possible on the very next move after the two-square pawn advance. If you do not take it immediately, the chance is gone.

questions.q: A pawn reaches the last rank. What may you do?
options: Only turn it into a queen
Turn it into a queen, rook, bishop or knight
Keep it as a pawn and move it sideways
questions.explain: You must promote, and you choose the piece. Choosing a knight (under-promotion) is sometimes the only winning or non-stalemating move.

questions.q: It is your opponent's turn. Their king is not in check and they have no legal move. What is the result?
options: You win by checkmate
It is a draw by stalemate
They must pass
questions.explain: No legal move and no check is stalemate: a draw. This is the classic way to spoil a winning position, so always leave the enemy king a move or give mate.

questions.q: The same position appears three times, with the same player to move. What can happen?
options: Nothing, repetition is not a rule
A player can claim a draw
The player who repeated loses
questions.explain: Threefold repetition lets a player claim a draw. The positions do not have to follow one another.

questions.q: Which ending is a draw because neither side can force checkmate?
options: King and rook against king
King and bishop against king
King and queen against king
questions.explain: King and a single minor piece cannot force mate against a lone king. King and rook, or king and queen, can.

questions.q: Can a king capture a piece that is protected by another enemy piece?
options: Yes, kings can capture anything
No, a king may not move to an attacked square
Only if the piece is a pawn
questions.explain: A king can never move to a square that an enemy piece attacks, which includes capturing a protected piece.

questions.q: You capture a rook (5) with your bishop (3), and they recapture the bishop with a pawn (1). What is the material result for you?
options: You are up 2
You are up 5
You are down 3
questions.explain: You gained 5 and lost 3, so you are up 2. Counting trades like this before you capture is the core of the Safety Check.
